What does the county take over after March 1?

Any balance still open on March 2 belongs to Oakland County, not the city, and the city's pay options no longer apply. Tax bills carry a notice if prior year taxes were returned delinquent, pointing the owner to the county treasurer's hardship line. Interest and penalties keep growing, so anyone selling a parcel with delinquent tax should clear it before listing or build the payoff into the closing statement.

For a deed with warranty covenants, state law has the register of deeds ask for a county treasurer certificate that no tax liens exist and that taxes for the five preceding years are paid (MCL 211.135). A quitclaim deed with no warranty is excepted from that rule. Either way, a clean tax history keeps a sale moving.

More questions about Rochester Hills, MI Property Tax Guide

Which number reaches the Rochester Hills assessor?

Dial 248-656-4605 for the Assessing Department. It handles values, name and address changes, and the Principal Residence Exemption. The office is at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive, inside City Hall.

What is the penalty if I miss the Rochester Hills summer deadline?

Interest of 1% attaches the day after the deadline and a further 1% attaches each month after that. The city also adds a 3% penalty after the mid-February winter deadline. Postmarks are not honored.

Does a sale change the next tax bill?

Yes. A transfer of ownership resets the taxable value to the state equalized value for the year after the sale. A buyer who inherits a long-held house can see a noticeably higher bill than the seller paid.

Can I pay my Rochester Hills tax bill by card?

Yes, online, by phone or at the Treasurer's office, with a 2.75% processing fee and a $1.50 minimum. E-check online is free. Checks go in the drop box at City Hall or by mail.

Where do delinquent Rochester Hills taxes go?

They go to the Oakland County Treasurer, 1200 N. Telegraph, Pontiac, MI 48341, from March 2. The county treasurer's number printed on the bill is 248-858-0611.

Which Westland office handles my property tax?

Call 734-467-3172 for tax billing or 734-467-3169 for Finance. City Hall staff are in from 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays. Values come from the Assessor's Office at the same address, phone 734-467-3160, which promises an answer within a business day.

Deeds are a different matter. They are filed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds in downtown Detroit and never at City Hall.

What are the Westland tax bill dates?

Bills leave the city on July 1 and December 1. Payment is expected by August 15 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter one, moving to the next business day if the date lands on a weekend, unless Council grants more time.

Where and how do Westland residents pay their taxes?

Options are the city's online payment portal, a phone service, and City Hall itself. Fees depend on the route.

How is a Westland home valued for tax?

Each year the Assessor sets a value for every parcel at 50% of true cash value as of December 31, the level state law requires. The bill itself multiplies taxable value, a different figure from assessed value, by the local millage rates, so a voter-approved millage change moves the bill even if the assessment holds still.

Three appraisal methods are described. Sales comparison looks at comparable homes that sold. The income method fits rentals. The 2026 assessments rely on sales from April 2023 through March 2025 and set aside bank sales and foreclosures as non-arm's-length deals.

A sale price cannot by itself justify a change. Neither the Assessor nor the Board of Review may raise or lower a value on price alone. The city posts its economic condition factor and land value studies, and an online lookup shows taxable value, balance owed, a parcel map and the legal description.

How do I contest a Westland assessment?

The March Board of Review is the route, and the city says it is the only time of year a residential value can be appealed. Notices arrive near the end of February, roughly two weeks before the board first sits, with hearing dates printed on them.

  • File a Petition to the Board of Review for every parcel, since incomplete ones are returned.
  • Appointments open only after notices are mailed and run five minutes each. A letter is allowed as an alternative.
  • Back your claim with an appraisal, comparable sales, a market analysis or photographs. Appointments and letters count equally, and the board decides later from the paper record.
  • Submit everything by 1:00 pm on the final scheduled meeting day.
  • A lawyer, accountant or agent may appear if both of you sign a written authorization.

Three members and two alternates serve, chosen by the Mayor and confirmed by Council. The board organizes on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March in the Council Chambers. It hears challenges to assessed value, poverty exemptions under MCL 211.7u and classification disputes, and fixes clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact.

The Wayne County Treasurer, at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit, takes over. According to the county, a bill still open at the local office after the last day of February turns delinquent on March 1 and can be paid only to the county from then on.

The county's timeline is blunt. A year of delinquency means forfeiture the following March 1, monthly interest moving from 1% to 1.5% back to the start, plus $175 for foreclosure and $30 for recording. At least ten written notices go out first, payment plans exist, and parcels that are foreclosed are offered to public bodies and then auctioned in September and October.

A seller with a balance can usually pay it from sale proceeds. Interest accrues monthly, so get a payoff figure from the Wayne County Treasurer before closing.

What does a Westland buyer or seller file after closing?

MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to tell the assessing office about the transfer on the state's form, showing the parties, the date, the real price and the parcel number. Title companies commonly hand out the form at closing.

Why it matters to the seller: taxable value is limited while one owner holds the home and then resets toward assessed value the year after a transfer, so the next owner's first bill can run well above yours. Anyone who claimed the principal residence exemption should file the state's rescind form for the property sold. Ask the Westland Assessor's Office for current forms and the status of your exemption.

What is Westland like as a place to sell?

Westland is a Detroit suburb roughly 18 miles west of downtown, covering 20.43 square miles of land. It grew out of Nankin Township, which filled in after World War II. The Norwayne subdivision, put up for returning soldiers who worked in nearby plants, is among its oldest neighborhoods. Westland Shopping Center opened in 1965, and township voters formed the city on May 16, 1966.

School assignments vary by street. Wayne-Westland Community Schools serve most of the city. The northern edge belongs to Livonia Public Schools, and small southern pockets are in Taylor and Romulus districts.

The Census Bureau estimates 82,333 residents for July 2025, versus 85,420 counted in 2020. Its 2020 to 2024 figures show 61.3% owner-occupied housing, a middle home value of $184,600, median gross rent of $1,158, and 35,932 households of about 2.30 people. Median household income is $62,076.

Wyoming by the numbers

Which Wyoming office collects property tax?

Payments go to the City Treasurer's Office inside City Hall at 1155 28th Street SW, Wyoming, MI 49509, which also bills water, sewer and other city charges. Wyoming is in Kent County. After March 1 the Kent County Treasurer handles real property tax that is still open.

The Assessor's Office tracks about 25,000 parcels, with owner names, mailing addresses, structure photos and sketches, permit lists and transfer histories. The assessor contact shown on the Board of Review page is 616-530-7231.

Drivers can use the window behind the building, staffed Monday to Thursday from 7:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.

What are the Wyoming tax due dates and penalties?

Wyoming sets summer taxes due on August 31 and winter taxes on February 14, and its Treasurer page lists what a late payment costs.

Unpaid real property tax is handed to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1. Business personal property tax is different: the city keeps it and adds 1% monthly until it is settled.

The summer penalty starts the day after August 31, so a closing near that date needs a title company that confirms which bill it paid.

What are the ways to pay Wyoming taxes?

Wyoming takes payment in person, by post, through a drop box and over the internet. Cash or a check brought to the Treasurer's Office adds no convenience fee.

  • Online payment runs through Invoice Cloud at wyomingmi.gov/payment. Cards carry 2.7% with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost $0.80.
  • Single card payments top out at $25,000, and e-checks at $125,000.
  • Accepted online: Discover, MasterCard, American Express and Visa, plus PayPal, Venmo and e-checks.
  • For mail, write the check to the City of Wyoming and enclose the stub or account number. A drop box is at the northeast entrance of City Hall.
  • Anything received after 5:00 PM counts the next day. Never mail or drop off cash.

To learn a parcel's balance before closing, call the Treasurer's Office or follow the property information link on its page.

How does Wyoming value a house for tax?

The city assesses real property at 50% of its usual selling price, as Michigan law directs. It runs a computer assisted mass appraisal system adjusted with current market data and halves true cash value to get assessed value.

The yearly calendar is public. Value notices are mailed on the last Friday of January. Complaints go to the assessor from the first Monday in February to the second Thursday, and the roll is certified on the first Monday in March. In 2026 the assessor's review closed on February 12 and the March Board of Review closed on March 12.

The city also lists every parcel by address with its current value and last sale price, in five alphabetical street ranges, so you can compare your house with neighbors before filing.

How can a Wyoming owner dispute an assessment?

Begin with the assessor's review in early February. If the answer is unsatisfying, the March Board of Review is the formal venue. Its executive session falls the day after the first Monday of March, hearings open the second Monday, and every review wraps up by the first Monday of April.

  • The board may increase, decrease or confirm a value. It can also add property left off the roll and grant poverty and principal residence exemptions that were missing last year.
  • The July and December meetings fix clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact. The assessor adds qualified agricultural exemptions, taxable uncappings and poverty exemptions to that list.
  • The Michigan Tax Tribunal is the next step, with filing deadlines of May 31 for commercial and industrial property and July 31 for residential.

City Council appoints members to three year terms. Each set includes a real estate practitioner, a public accountant and a property owner who has been in the city at least a year.

Which other Wyoming assessing dates should an owner mark?

The assessor's calendar lists several dates beyond the March appeals. February 1 is the deadline for the qualified business form L-4143, and February 20 is the deadline for personal property statements (Form 632), small business property tax exemption claims (Form 5076) and the eligible manufacturing personal property affidavit (Form 5278).

  • First Monday in March: the assessor certifies the assessment roll.
  • Wednesday after the first Monday in April: the Board of Review roll goes to Kent County.
  • June 1: principal residence exemption affidavits for the summer bill.
  • November 1: the same affidavits for the winter bill.
  • December 31: tax day, which fixes the condition of a property for the next year's assessment.

Boards of Review judge a property by the facts that existed on tax day.

Which exemptions change when a Wyoming house is sold?

Under the principal residence exemption, an owner-occupied home is relieved of as much as 18 mills of school operating tax. A buyer must own and live in the home by June 1 to have it on the summer bill, or by November 1 for the winter bill, and a later move-in waits for the next tax year. The city says a form may have been signed at closing and that anyone unsure should file one with the Assessor's Office.

Only one such exemption is allowed per person, so the seller's old homestead needs a rescind form before a new one can be granted. Disabled veterans can claim a separate exemption using Form 5107 with Veterans Affairs paperwork, and the city asks for a copy of a driver's license.

A transfer affidavit is due from the buyer within 45 days, and Wyoming says missing it can bring back tax from the transfer date with penalties and interest. For an existing owner, taxable value is held down by the cap. A sale lifts it to assessed value the following year, so a new owner often sees a larger first bill.

What should a seller know about Wyoming itself?

After Grand Rapids, which touches it on the northeast, Wyoming is West Michigan's second largest city. It began as a farm township organized in 1848 and incorporated as a city in 1959 after annexation fights with Grand Rapids and Grandville. The 28th Street corridor, anchored by Rogers Plaza and Studio 28, became a regional shopping strip. Growth then drifted southwest to RiverTown Crossings. General Motors shut its stamping plant in 2009, and the 74 acre site, now called Site 36, is a redevelopment focus.

Census Bureau figures: 78,588 residents in the July 2025 estimate, against 76,501 in 2020, living on 24.74 square miles of land. Among 2020 to 2024 results, 67.1% of homes are owner-occupied, owned homes have a middle value of $225,200, and rent runs $1,196 at the median. There are 29,417 households of 2.61 people each, with a median income of $73,677 and a 21.9 minute average commute.

Yes. A drive-up window behind City Hall is staffed Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. There is also a drop box at the northeast entrance, and online payment carries a fee.

The Kent County Treasurer collects delinquent real property tax from that date. Personal property tax stays at the city, with 1% interest each month.

Early February for the assessor's review, then the March Board of Review, which opens hearings on the second Monday of March. Residential owners may go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by July 31.
